snippet.title: Greenhouse Wood Stove, Grouse Hunt & Fast Approaching Winter Weather
snippet.description:
After building a small concrete block wall for holding firewood we install our wood stove piping for the greenhouse, then it's time to pour the concrete footings for our wood shed, we get it done just before the snow flies. Work hard, play hard - we spend a day of exploring, grouse hunting and berry picking only to return home and finish up closing down the greenhouse for the year. We welcome winter's arrival with grouse cranberry sourdough sandwiches.

We appreciate you tagging along for our Alaskan adventure 😀

Thank you for watching and supporting our channel! 💙
- Eric & Arielle

snippet.title: Ice Fishing with my Wife and Cali | Canadian Winter Homesteading
snippet.description:
Out on the ice with my girls.Nothing quite like a quiet winter day — just me, my wife, and our golden retriever exploring the frozen lake. Started the morning in the warm cabin sharpening up the old knife while Cali kept me company, sticking her nose right in there like she always does.
Then we headed out across the ice, sled in tow, with Cali leading the way, tail going a mile a minute. She loves this life as much as we do. We stopped by the big frozen waterfall, had a little snack, and I gave Cali a few treats for being such a good adventure partner.
These are the days that fill the soul. Simple, cold, and beautiful. Just the way I like it.
Cali says thanks for coming along on the journey with us.

snippet.title: Lake Erie, Ohio walleye Catch and Cook \ Ep.3 On the Ice Season 2 The Road Trip
snippet.description:
Head to https://drinkag1.com/fowlersmakeryandmischief to get an AG1 Flavor Sampler and a bottle of Vitamin D3+K2 FREE in your Welcome Kit with your first AG1 subscription (a $72 value!).”

In this episode of the On the Ice series, I made an unexpected stop on Lake Erie after discovering the lake had completely frozen over — something that hasn’t happened like this in decades. Instead of heading straight to Chicago, I met up with local outfitters near Rattlesnake Island and rented one of their ice fishing shacks to try my luck at some legendary Lake Erie walleye fishing.

Day one of ice fishing on Lake Erie started slow, and after miles of driving across the frozen lake I managed to land just a single fish. But I wasn’t ready to give up yet.

On day two, I loaded up the SnowDog and chased the walleye across the ice for miles. After exploring farther west across the lake, about an hour from where I started the first day, I finally found the fish and got into some great Lake Erie walleye fishing action.

With an unusual warm spell pushing temperatures close to 60 degrees, I packed up, headed back to shore, and pulled everything out of the trailer in the parking lot for a Catch and Cook, cooking up fresh Lake Erie walleye in the sunshine after a great couple of days ice fishing Lake Erie.

After the adventure on the ice, it was time to pack up and continue the journey.

Next stop: Chicago and Milwaukee, chasing big brown trout in Episode 4 of the On the Ice adventure series.

snippet.title: Soil Biology in Dryland Cropping Explained
snippet.description:
Can soil biology help farmers grow crops with less rain and fewer inputs? Today we're in South Australia with the Schutz family to see what changes they're seeing in the paddock and inside the tractor cab.

The surprising results aren't just about soil structure — they're changing fuel use, resilience and how the whole farm system performs.

Today we're back with the Schutz family on their 4,500-hectare cropping operation in South Australia. Gary "Squirt" Schutz explains how increasing soil biological activity and changing management practices have affected soil structure, diesel use, equipment life, moisture retention and crop resilience.

This isn't a story about abandoning fertiliser or chemistry. It's about balance — combining biological farming principles with practical cropping systems to build healthier soils while improving long-term performance.

Useful for:

• Broadacre farmers
• Dryland croppers
• Regenerative agriculture practitioners
• Mixed farming businesses
• Anyone interested in soil health and resilient farming systems

Topics covered include soil biology, moisture retention, dryland farming, soil structure, regenerative agriculture, crop resilience, biological farming systems and practical farming strategies in marginal rainfall environments.

snippet.title: How to Set Up a Solar Electric Fence Energizer
snippet.description:
Your energizer isn’t just the power source — it’s the brain of your electric fence system.
Set it up wrong, and even the best fence will underperform.

Join this channel to get access to perks:
https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCdtlC5DtsgZKCM8gislyDJw/join

In this video, I’m at the Gippsland Agricultural Group Research Centre with Gallagher Technical Lead Noel Hecker walking step-by-step through how to properly install a solar-powered electric fence energizer system.

We cover:
• Choosing the right energizer size
• Solar panel setup and bracket orientation
• Battery wiring and fuse safety
• Installing an app gateway for remote monitoring
• Lightning diverters and system protection
• Weatherproof mounting tips
• Running lead-out cable safely
• Avoiding common installation mistakes

If you’re running livestock, managing rotational grazing, or building multi-wire electric fencing across kilometres of country, this setup matters. A correctly installed solar energizer means reliable voltage, fewer stock breakouts, less time troubleshooting, and stronger fence performance year-round.

This is especially useful for:
• Farmers running large paddock systems
• Off-grid properties
• Regenerative grazing setups
• Contractors installing electric fencing
• Anyone upgrading from small solar units to larger systems

Electric fencing performance depends on system design — energizer output (joules), battery capacity, solar input, earthing, lightning protection, and correct installation all work together. This video explains the full system thinking behind it.
